partQuestions.1: Why can environmental decisions rarely rest on a single stage, and how do early container studies and modern LCA frameworks divide methodological responsibility?
partQuestions.2: How do you frame study goal and scope, draw foreground versus background boundaries, anchor a fair functional reference, and close linear and hybrid inventories?
partQuestions.3: When processes yield co-products, shift marginal supply, draw from dynamic grids, or enter recycling loops, how should burdens be partitioned or credited?
partQuestions.4: How do emissions, land use, and resource extractions translate into midpoint and endpoint indicators across climate, stratospheric ozone and radiation, acidification and eutrophication, particulate matter and photochemical ozone, water, toxicity, and resources?
partQuestions.5: Where do multi-criteria trade-offs, spatial regionalization, monetary valuation, social risk scales, and life cycle costing hit their interpretive limits?
partQuestions.6: How did major background LCA databases evolve, why do their underlying methods diverge, and why do elementary flows and processes resist lossless cross-database mapping?
partQuestions.7: How do dataset applicability, uncertainty propagation, pedigree ratings, and statutory product-footprint rules constrain what conclusions a study can legitimately support?
partQuestions.8: Returning to worked wall-service, carrier-bag, and prospective technology cases, how can you audit an LCA comparison and revise specific steps when new evidence arrives?

readingModes.title: Sequential Study (Foundations & Courses)
readingModes.audience: Readers new to life cycle assessment and graduate-level courses
readingModes.description: Start with the Preface and Reading Guide, then move straight through the parts in order—from early beverage-container ledgers to background databases, data quality, and full comparative cases.

readingModes.title: Problem-First Lookup (Practitioners & Reviewers)
readingModes.audience: Experienced LCA modelers and critical reviewers checking specific methodological boundaries
readingModes.description: Jump straight to any recurring modeling or review question below, paired with the Concept Index and References to inspect primary-source divergences.

readingModes.title: Case-First Reverse Reading (Empirical Entry)
readingModes.audience: Readers who prefer to examine a complete numerical comparison before unpacking theory
readingModes.description: Open with Wall Service Comparison and Carrier-Bag Studies, then trace links and chapter notes back to functional units, matrix balancing, background databases, climate metrics, and review rules.

problemRoutes.question: Building a product carbon footprint or preparing for EU Battery Regulation / ESPR compliance—where should I start?
problemRoutes.summary: Clarify functional vs. declared units, fossil vs. biogenic carbon rules, secondary-data thresholds, and statutory comparative-assertion gates.

problemRoutes.question: How do I choose between allocation, system expansion, and recycling formulas (including CFF) without double counting?
problemRoutes.summary: Separate attributional burden-sharing from consequential marginal substitution, and verify electricity scales and recycling handover rules.

problemRoutes.question: Why does switching impact assessment methods or weighting sets flip the ranking of the exact same inventory?
problemRoutes.summary: Trace midpoint vs. endpoint cut-offs, regionalized characterization, normalization-denominator dilution, and value-choice weighting mechanisms.

targets.why: LCIA structure, midpoints/endpoints & six method families

problemRoutes.question: How should I choose a background database, handle cross-database mapping limits, and interpret data quality and uncertainty?
problemRoutes.summary: Navigate global database families, elementary-flow and process mapping redlines, dataset applicability, pedigree ratings, and Monte Carlo limits.

problemRoutes.question: Assessing lab-scale technologies or 2030/2050 decarbonization pathways—what are the main pitfalls in prospective LCA?
problemRoutes.summary: Distinguish process scale-up, IAM-coupled superstructure background scenarios, and dynamic timing boundaries along with their validation limits.

problemRoutes.question: Given a published comparative LCA report, how can I test whether its conclusions actually hold up?
problemRoutes.summary: Use worked arithmetic cases and government assessments to audit comparative-assertion eligibility, hotspot thresholds, and critical-review boundaries.
